In Brett Baker, Ilana Mushin, Mark Harvey & Rod Gardner (eds), Indigenous language and social identity: papers in honour of Michael Walsh (Pacific Linguistics 626), 79-104. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. [hdl 1885/146773, open access]
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.5 'The linguistic evidence for Yukul' (pp. 85ff.): 'We have almost nothing in the way of positive identifications of language material with the name Yukul'; the only material is two anonymous 1872 wordlists (Crowder, 10 words; Lowrie in Curr 1886-87, ~70 words) attributed to Yukul by triangulation and found to be Marra-like; conclusion (p. ~91): 'linguistically it was very similar to Marra'. No phonology, no prosody.
